Diego,

Thanks for the earlier call. Legal Ops asked me to capture the two outstanding items before we proceed to signature: (1) a short mapping explaining whether Acme (customer) or Redwood is the Controller for telemetry/usage logs and embeddings-derived artifacts, and (2) retention windows + access controls for logs that contain customer prompts and derived embeddings.

We tried to keep changes minimal in the DPA; attached is our mark-up (Redwood-DPA_v3.2_acme-redlines.pdf). Our priority is: auditability (we need logs for 12 months), clear obligations if Redwood retains embeddings, and a carve-out for telemetry used solely for performance optimization (we're OK with aggregated telemetry).

Can you confirm Redwood's view on: controller/processor mapping for telemetry (including logs that contain raw prompts), and whether Redwood will treat embeddings as "derived data" that remains subject to customer deletion requests?

Tom
Legal Ops — Acme Corp

From: Diego Fernández <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@acme-corp.com>, Sarah O'Neill <soneill@vendorsecure.io>

Subject: Re: Privacy definitions for telemetry / embeddings

Tom — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. I reviewed with Product and Privacy; summarizing Redwood's positions so we can put the right language in the DPA and move to eSign: 

1) Controller vs Processor mapping: Redwood will be Processor for customer-provided content (prompts, files) and any embeddings generated from that content. Acme will be Controller for the original content and for decisions about legal basis. For telemetry (runtime logs that include request metadata and, in some cases, redacted prompt snippets), Redwood acts as Processor when those logs are collected under the hosting of Acme's account. We can accept a limited Processor+subprocessor role statement that clarifies this mapping (we will not assert Controller status).

2) Embeddings: Embeddings derived from customer content are treated as "Customer Data" (i.e., covered by the DPA). We will support deletion requests: when Acme requests deletion, Redwood will delete embeddings and purge any caching/KV entries within 30 days unless retention is needed for compliance or active dispute. We'll document exceptions (e.g., backups) and retention timing.

3) Telemetry & logs: We can provide a 12-month retention option (on by request for enterprise customers) and standard 90-day retention for hosted customers. Access controls: logs that include prompt content will be restricted to a small SRE/infra access group with audit logging and SOC 2 controls. Aggregated telemetry used purely for performance optimization will be retained indefinitely in aggregated form and is not reversible to customer prompts.

Next steps: I attached a short internal mapping diagram (acme-telemetry-dataflow.png) and am happy to accept the three redlines you mentioned with one small edit to the deletion clause (to allow 30-day purge window). If that works, I can upload the agreed DPA to DocuSign and share the envelope link.

Diego Fernández
